De’Anthony Melton (back, left-sided stiffness) is out for Saturday’s game against the Hawks.

Melton’s absence means that Matisse Thybulle moves into the starting lineup. While a very good defender, Thybulle’s limited offensive game means that the risk outweighs the reward when considering whether or not to roster him. Tyrese Maxey, Tobias Harris, P.J. Tucker, and Joel Embiid complete the starting lineup.

    De’Anthony Melton (back; left-sided stiffness) has been added to the injury report as questionable ahead of Saturday’s rematch with the Hawks.

    Melton has been the starter with James Harden sidelined, so if he misses this game, Doc Rivers will likely be deciding between Shake Milton and Matisse Thybulle as the starter. Thybulle is an excellent defender, but Milton can provide both scoring and playmaking, which they may opt for in the starting unit. Both guys would be utilized extra, but whichever starts will likely receive the bigger boost.

  • James Harden

    CLE Guard #1
    Player Stats
    Link copied to clipboard!

    James Harden (right foot tendon sprain) is wearing a walking boot and can’t put weight on his foot for at least the first week of his recovery.

    Sixers coach Doc Rivers was blunt about the challenges facing Harden as he rehabs his foot. “He can’t come back and be 10 pounds heavier or whatever,” Rivers said. “It’s hard not to be. I would be.” Adrian Wojnarowski reports that Harden is “expected” to miss one month, though Philly is due to re-evaluate him in a few weeks. Joel Embiid will enjoy even more usage without Harden, as will Tyrese Maxey, and the Sixers will shift some minutes to Shake Milton and Furkan Korkmaz. But the biggest winner may be De’Anthony Melton, who is already hitting top-75 value (9-cat) in a mere 23.3 minutes per game.

    De’Anthony Melton missed a potential game-winner at the end of Friday’s loss to the Knicks, finishing 4-of-18 from the field for 12 points, a game-high nine assists, five rebounds, three 3-pointers, two steals and two blocks.

    Melton is currently available in 30% of Yahoo leagues, a number that should be zero. James Harden’s strained right foot tendon will cost him a minimum of two weeks, and Adrian Wojnarowski reports that he’s “expected to miss a month.” That leaves his 36.7 minutes per game up for grabs, along with 27% usage and 93.0 touches per game (second in the NBA behind Tyrese Haliburton and Nikola Jokic). Melton is an obvious beneficiary, and has the defensive chops to be a top-75 player even if his offense isn’t flowing. Enjoy the ride.

    Source: ESPN.com

    James Harden (right foot tendon strain) is expected to miss one month, per ESPN’s Adrian Wojnarowski.

    Harden injured his left leg on Wednesday night, but this is unrelated. It’s unclear when this happened, but the 76ers will have to figure out other ways to score. While the initial report had Harden being sidelined for a month, the 76ers announced that he’ll be re-evaluated in two weeks. Joel Embiid should be back soon, but this seems like a golden opportunity for both Tyrese Maxey and De’Anthony Melton to see more playmaking and scoring opportunities. Matisse Thybulle started with both Melton and Embiid sidelined against Washington, so we’ll see who Doc Rivers ultimately decides to bump into the starting unit.

    Source: Adrian Wojnarowski on Twitter

    Joel Embiid is questionable for Wednesday’s matchup with Washington due to a non-COVID illness.

    Embiid was held out Monday for the illness, and there’s a chance he misses a second straight game. De’Anthony Melton has started in Embiid’s place in both games the big man has missed thus far, and Melton has averaged 14.5 points, 3.5 boards, 3.5 dimes, 3.5 steals and 1.5 triples in those contests. He’ll likely be in line for another start if Embiid sits this one out.

    De’Anthony Melton got the start Monday in place of Joel Embiid and racked up 16 points, two rebounds, two steals and an assist.

    He shot 7-of-10 from the field and connected on 2-of-4 three-point attempts as well. It was a nice showing for Melton who went 13/5/6 with five steals when he started against Toronto on October 28. After a slow start to his Philadelphia campaign, the preseason sleeper has finally started to deliver for fantasy managers who selected him with a late-round draft pick. On Halloween night, he might not be the full-sized candy bar, but he’s certainly not the miniature dental floss anymore.
